thread.title: Missouri Judge Rules Against Congressional Redistricting Referendum
thread.title_full: Missouri Judge Rules Against Congressional Redistricting Referendum

title: Missouri Judge Rules Against Congressional Redistricting Referendum
text:
• A Missouri judge ruled that the state's referendum process cannot be used to challenge congressional maps drawn by the Legislature.
• The ruling allows a new GOP-friendly map to remain in place for November's midterm elections.
• The judge sided with Republican Secretary of State Denny Hoskins in a closely watched fight over a Trump-backed map.
• The map could help determine control of the U.S. House.
• The judge ruled that Hoskins' decision not to certify the referendum petition was "lawful".
• The Republican-backed congressional map "remains in full force and effect for the 2026 general election".
• Plaintiff Richard von Glahn appealed the ruling.
• The new boundaries are aimed at giving Republicans an opportunity to defeat Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver of Kansas City.
• Missouri's current eight-member House delegation consists of six Republicans and two Democrats.
• The map splits portions of Kansas City between neighboring Republican-held districts.
• The remainder of Cleaver's 5th Congressional District stretches into Republican-heavy rural areas.
• About 59% of voters in the reshaped district are new to it.
• Republican state Sen. Rick Brattin won the GOP primary in the redrawn district.
• Cleaver was unopposed for the Democratic nomination.
• The new boundaries were already used in Missouri's August primaries.
• Opponents collected thousands of signatures seeking to force a statewide referendum on the map.
• Hoskins rejected the petition, arguing that Missouri's Constitution does not allow congressional redistricting to be put to a referendum.
• The Missouri fight is part of a broader national redistricting battle ahead of November's elections.
• Republican Gov. Mike Kehoe called lawmakers into a special session last year after Trump urged Republican-led states to redraw congressional boundaries.
• Missouri became the second Republican-led state, after Texas, to pursue new congressional boundaries as part of that push.
• Green's ruling leaves the Trump-backed map in place while the case moves to the appeals court.
summary: Cole County Circuit Judge Daniel Green ruled Wednesday that Missouri's constitutional referendum provisions "do not apply to congressional redistricting enacted by the General Assembly," siding with Republican Secretary of State Denny Hoskins in a closely watched fight over a Trump-backed map that could help determine control of the U.S. House. Green also ruled that Hoskins' decision not to certify the referendum petition was "lawful" and ordered that the Republican-backed congressional map "remains in full force and effect for the 2026 general election."
